chunks.arabic_text: غَالٍ، خَطَّابِيٌّ، كُوفِيٌّ يَضَعُ الْحَدِيثَ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ)

translations.en: A ghālī, a Khaṭṭābī. Kufan. He fabricates ḥadīth. He narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him)

en.summary: Yunus ibn Bahman, a Kufan narrator of Imam al-Sadiq, is characterized in al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitab al-Du'afā* as a *ghālī* (exaggerator) and *khaṭṭābī* (one who speaks independently), indicating his tendency to attribute excessive or independent theological claims to the Imam. His status as a fabricator (*yadhu al-hadīth*) highlights the critical Shia methodology of distinguishing between authentic transmission and the doctrinal innovations that emerged in Kufa during the late Imams period.
en.seo_question: Who is Yunus ibn Bahman and what are his characteristics in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالٍ: Ghali: One who exaggerates the virtues or status of the Imams, often to the point of divinity.
key_terms.خَطَّابِيٌّ: Khattabi: One who speaks freely or excessively, often implying independent opinion or eloquence without strict adherence.
key_terms.يَضَعُ الْحَدِيثَ: Yada'u al-hadith: He fabricates or invents hadith.
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abi Abdillah: The title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
